$comment: Curated map from raw registry parameter names (capability_profile.parameter)
to the standard parameters seeded into CalibrationParameterStandards.
This file is REVIEWED INPUT, not generated output. scripts/build_parameter_standards.py
consumes it and fails if any raw name in the registry is unmapped, so new registry
versions cannot silently introduce unseeded parameters.
Every entry carries 'review': entries marked true are metrology judgment calls that
need engineer sign-off before seeding. Entries marked false are mechanical
(case duplicates, unit spellings) and safe as-is.
subtypeKind distinguishes the three unrelated things the registry stores in
capability_profile.subtype, so the UI can label the selector correctly.

unitAliases.$comment: raw unit -> canonical unit. Applied to profile units before seeding.

$comment: Unit pairs that look like duplicates but may be metrologically distinct.
Not merged automatically - a gauge-referenced unit is not the same quantity
as its absolute counterpart.
unitsNeedingReview.mbar g vs mbar: 'g' suffix denotes gauge reference, not a spelling variant. Kept distinct.
unitsNeedingReview.bar g vs bar: Same. 'Gauge Pressure' is modelled as its own parameter.

subtypeKinds.gauge_dimension: 24.00mm/24.12mm/... - physical size of the gauge artifact, NOT an element type

parameters.$comment: raw registry name -> standard definition. 'merged' entries fold into another standardName.

Type-J thermocouple simulation.rationale: Duplicates Thermocouple+subtype for source-role instruments. Folding removes 6 redundant standards. Confirm the simulation ranges are equivalent to the element ranges.

Temperature.note: Registry category is ['Mechanical','Source','Thermal'] - 'Source' is a role value leaking into the category field. Normalized to Thermal.

Temperature indicator.rationale: Describes the instrument's function (indicator), not a distinct measured quantity. Same unit and overlapping range as Temperature.

Temperature sensor.rationale: As above. If the lab reports indicator and sensor separately on certificates, keep them split instead.

Temperature Generation.rationale: 'Generation' implies source role, but the registry tags it measuring. Likely a role-inference bug upstream - confirm before folding.

Temperature - Type K sensor.rationale: Ambiguous: could be Thermocouple/Type K, or a Temperature measurement that merely happens to use a Type K probe. Range -50..250 is narrow for a Type K element.

Dew Point Temperature.note: Distinct derived quantity - not folded into Temperature.

Relative Humidity Generation.rationale: Same 'Generation' role-leak pattern as Temperature Generation.

Gauge Pressure.rationale: Not anticipated by the scope doc. Kept distinct because 'bar g' is gauge-referenced. Confirm the lab treats it as its own parameter rather than Pressure with a reference flag.

Compression Force.rationale: EVIDENCE-BACKED, not a guess: assets 219 and 746 are both Digital Force Gauges declaring asset-level 'Force', but 219's profiles are [Force - pull mode, Force - push mode] while 746's are [Compression Force, Tension Force]. The registry describes the same instrument type both ways, so push == compression. Review is a formality unless the lab reports them separately on certificates.

Force - push mode.rationale: See Compression Force. Note ranges differ (0-20 vs 0-100 kgf) - merging widens the standard's observed range, which affects pre-filtering eligibility.

Tension Force.rationale: EVIDENCE-BACKED by the same asset 219/746 comparison: pull == tension. See Compression Force.

Force - pull mode.rationale: See Tension Force. Ranges differ (0-100 vs 0-20 kgf).

Speed (Contact).note: Scope doc explicitly requires Contact/Non-Contact to stay separate.

Speed.rationale: Bare 'Speed' cannot be assigned to Contact or Non-Contact from the registry alone. Left as its own standard pending inspection of the 2 owning assets; do not auto-merge.

Air Flow.rationale: No unit and no buckets in the registry. Cannot participate in accuracy filtering. Confirm whether this is a real capability or an extraction gap.

Flow.rationale: Generic 'Flow' (SLPM) alongside three medium-specific flow parameters. Confirm whether it should fold into one of them.

Acceleration.note: Added by scripts/apply_certificate_findings.py from asset 600's certificate (Vibration Meter, acceleration mode 0.1-400 m/s²). Not present in the original registry extraction.

Displacement.rationale: Added from asset 600's certificate (vibration displacement, peak-to-peak, 0.001-4.000 mm). Note that assets 44 and 45 also carry 'Displacement'/'Length' as their CERTIFICATE parameter while their profile parameter is 'Thickness' - confirm whether dial-gauge displacement and vibration displacement are the same standard.

CO2.note: Promoted from proposedNewStandards once asset 755's certificate supplied range (0-100000 ppm) and accuracy (±1%).

Ultra Vacuum.note: Promoted from proposedNewStandards once asset 742's certificate supplied the unit (mbar) and the ±10% acceptance criterion.

Velocity.rationale: KEEP AS 'Velocity'. An earlier draft proposed renaming this to 'Vibration Velocity'; the source spreadsheet overrules that. 'MASTER LIST AS PER SOP & PARAMETER.xlsx' records PARAMETER='Velocity' for BOTH vibration meters (374, 600) - 'Vibration Velocity' appears only in the registry's asset-level parameters[], where the parser enriched the lab's term. Renaming would depart from the lab's own SOP document. If the lab prefers the longer name, that belongs in the per-org customName, not the standard.

Time.rationale: No unit, no buckets. Likely should fold into Time Interval - confirm against the owning asset.

Mass.note: Asset-level vocabulary calls this 'Weight' (10 assets). Alias recorded in assetLevelAliases.

Sound Pressure Level.note: Asset-level vocabulary calls this 'Sound Intensity' - metrologically NOT the same quantity, but they refer to the same instruments here.

Light Intensity.rationale: Categorised Mechanical in the registry; lux is photometric. Category likely wrong.

Particle Count.rationale: Unit is µm (a size threshold), not a count. No buckets. Unit semantics need confirming.

Level / Inclination.rationale: No unit, no buckets. Sole owner is a Granite Surface Plate.

Flatness.rationale: subtype holds gauge-block sizes (24.00mm...), not an element type. The subtype selector must be labelled per subtypeKind or this renders nonsensically.

$comment: asset.parameters[] names with no profile-level counterpart, so legacy
certificates and asset-level labels still resolve to a seeded standard.
Each entry was verified by locating every asset declaring the name and
inspecting that same asset's capability profiles. 'evidence' records that
check as (records supporting the mapping)/(records declaring the name).
resolvesTo is a LIST: some asset-level names legitimately expand to more
than one standard. An empty list means no profile coverage exists.
confidence: high   - every owning record agrees
medium - agrees where profiles exist, but coverage is partial
low    - owning records disagree; do not rely on this alias

Weight.note: Every one of the 10 declaring records has exactly one profile, 'Mass'.

Dew Point.note: Asset 564 (Dew Point Transmitter), sole parameter to sole profile.

Sound Intensity.note: 3/3 in the registry AND all 3 spreadsheet rows say 'Sound Intensity'. The profile-level name is the INFERRED correction - physically, a dB sound level meter measures sound pressure level, not sound intensity (W/m^2). So the standard should be 'Sound Pressure Level' and this lab's customName should default to 'Sound Intensity'.

Power.note: Asset 153 (Digital Power Meter). The spreadsheet says only 'POWER'; 'Three-phase' was inferred by the capability matrix, not declared by the lab. Narrows generic->specific, so adding a single-phase power meter later would silently break this alias. Verify the three-phase claim against the instrument before seeding.

Vibration Velocity.note: CORRECTED against the spreadsheet. Both vibration meters (374, 600) record PARAMETER='Velocity' there; 'Vibration Velocity' exists only in the registry's asset-level parameters[], added by the parser. The alias holds, but do NOT rename the standard - see the 'Velocity' entry under parameters.

Force.note: Expands to both directions. The two declaring assets are both Digital Force Gauges but are described differently: 219 has [Force - pull mode, Force - push mode] while 746 has [Compression Force, Tension Force]. This is direct evidence that push == compression and pull == tension, and independently supports the Force merges in 'parameters' above.

AC/DC Voltage.note: Expands to both, but per-asset coverage varies and the label overstates it: asset 63 (True RMS Multimeter) has only AC profiles, asset 149 only DC Voltage. Asset 165 has no profiles at all. Resolving to both will over-report capability for those assets - prefer the profile-level name whenever one exists.

AC/DC Current.note: Same pattern and the same caveat as AC/DC Voltage.

Level.note: DO NOT RELY ON THIS. Only asset 46 (Spirit Level) maps cleanly. Asset 35 (Granite Surface Plate) has zero profiles. Asset 266 (Bevel Protractor) declares [Level, Angle] but its only profile is Angle, so 'Level' there resolves to nothing.
Level.rootCause: The spreadsheet uses inconsistent separators in the PARAMETER column: asset 46 reads 'Level , Angle' (comma) while asset 266 reads 'Level / Angle' (slash). The parser treated both as two parameters, but a slash may well denote one combined 'Level/Angle' capability - which is also how the profile name 'Level / Inclination' is spelled. Resolve the separator semantics in the source data rather than patching it downstream.

CO2.note: RESOLVED from the spreadsheet. Asset 755 (CO2 Transmitter) has zero capability profiles, but its Range cell reads '0 to 1,00,000 ppm' - a complete, unambiguous range once Indian digit grouping is handled. See proposedNewStandards.CO2.

Volume.note: RESOLVED as spurious - do NOT create a Volume standard. Asset 602 (Standard Weight box) lists PARAMETER 'Weight, Volume', but its Range cell reads '1mg to 200g', which is purely a mass span. There is no volume range anywhere in the source. The registry giving 602 only a Mass profile was correct; 'Volume' looks like a data-entry artifact in the spreadsheet (possibly noted because weights displace volume for buoyancy correction). Recommend removing it from the source spreadsheet.

Ultra Vacuum.note: PARTIALLY RESOLVED from the spreadsheet. Asset 742 (Digital Hi.Pr. Pirani Gauge) has zero profiles; its Range cell reads '103 to 10-3', which is 10^3 to 10^-3 with the superscripts lost in the spreadsheet - so 0.001 to 1000. The UNIT is not stated anywhere and cannot be inferred safely; a Pirani gauge is typically mbar or Torr, and those differ by a factor of ~1.33. The unit must come from the lab or from SOP NLAB/CAL/ML14/R01 before this is seeded. See proposedNewStandards['Ultra Vacuum'].

$comment: Standards that do NOT exist in capability_profiles but are justified by the
source spreadsheet. Without these, the owning assets can never appear as
eligible masters for their declared parameter.
Both are range-only: the spreadsheet has no accuracy or least-count column, so
they participate in RANGE filtering but not ACCURACY filtering until a
calibration certificate supplies bucket data.

evidence.certificateAppendix: capability_appendix entry 'CO2 concentration capability' reads '0 to 100000 ppm (10%) CO2' - independently confirms the spreadsheet range.

warnings: The certificate also covers a SECOND parameter the registry did not record: Temp 0 to 50 deg C. The transmitter measures temperature as well as CO2. Added as profile P2 by apply_certificate_findings.py.
This asset is OVERDUE (valid till 20.03.26; 166 days overdue at the registry snapshot).
CO2.rangeSemanticsNote: An earlier draft of this file treated the 25,000 ppm top span-gas point as a cap on usable range and flagged the declared 100,000 ppm as a traceability problem. That was WRONG. Per the lab: the DECLARED range is the capability, and calibration points are samples within it - the accuracy established at the outermost points extends to the declared limits. So the capability is the full 0-100,000 ppm at ±1%. calibratedRange below is retained for reference only, not as a filter bound.
CO2.note: Certificate-verified. Accuracy is +/-1% of reading - note the capability_appendix recorded '0.0% error', which is the OBSERVED error, not the accuracy limit. The registry's range_parsed is WRONG ({min:0, max:1.0, unit:',00,000'}) - the extractor split on the first comma of the Indian-grouped number, which its own merge_issues already flags.

evidence.description: Digital Hi.Pr. Pirani Gauge (HHV, DHPG-222 / HPS-2)
evidence.certificateAppendix: capability_appendix entry 'Vacuum pressure' reads 'Approximately 1 x 10^-3 to 1 x 10^3 mbar (as printed)'.

verifiedAgainstCertificate.instrument: DIG HI PRE PIRANI, model DHPG-222 with gauge head HPS-2, Sl.No 525/61
verifiedAgainstCertificate.acceptanceCriteria: Pirani gauge +/-10% of the Master gauge - ACCEPTED

warnings: The +/-10% figure is an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (the tolerance used for the pass/fail decision), not a manufacturer accuracy specification. It is also very coarse: a master with +/-10% gives a poor test uncertainty ratio for calibrating other vacuum gauges. Confirm before relying on it for pre-filtering.
Ultra Vacuum.note: UNIT CONFIRMED FROM THE CERTIFICATE FACE - 'Range: 1 x 10^3 To 1x10^-3 m.bar'. Not inferred. The certificate also confirms the 10^-3..10^3 reading of the spreadsheet's mangled '103 to 10-3'. IMPORTANT: this is NOT range-only as previously recorded - capability_appendix says accuracy NOT_STATED, but the certificate carries a +/-10% acceptance criterion. The registry's range_parsed remains wrong ({min:103, max:10, unit:'-3'}); its own merge_issues already identifies this as an upstream scientific-notation parsing failure.
